views.name: Request path and base install
views.text: A client calls the gateway on the published port, and the gateway sends the request to a provider.

views.name: Codex services and the quota router
views.text: Up to three ChatGPT accounts run in their own proxies, and the automatic route prefers codex3, then codex2, then codex1.

views.name: Copilot service
views.text: One GitHub Copilot account runs in the separate service copilot, and the gateway calls it on the project network.

views.name: Decision router for model=auto
views.text: A pre-call hook asks a decision service and applies five rules in order to set the model of a request for auto.

views.name: Image build and release
views.text: Work flows from topic branches to local-dev, a checked snapshot goes to portable, and a release tag builds the image.

views.name: Host configuration layers
views.text: Tracked files hold a generic stack, and each host adds its own values in files that Git ignores.

nodes.label: client
nodes.summary: A client sends an OpenAI-compatible request to the gateway. The request carries a LiteLLM key. The gateway refuses a request without a valid key.
facts: the master key or a virtual key

nodes.summary: Compose publishes port 4000 of gateway on this address. It is the only published port of the stack. GATEWAY_PORT in .env changes the address.

nodes.label: reverse proxy
nodes.summary: A public address, for example https://<domain>, needs a reverse proxy. The proxy joins the external network proxy and forwards to litellm:4000. docs/examples/Caddyfile.fragment is an example route for Caddy.

nodes.label: .env
nodes.summary: The secrets and the host settings of one checkout, with mode 0600. Compose reads it for each ${VAR} and gives each key to gateway. Git ignores it.

nodes.label: config/gateway.example.yaml
nodes.summary: The tracked default configuration of gateway. It has two routes: openrouter/* and local/example-model. Compose mounts it when GATEWAY_CONFIG is not set.

nodes.label: .local/config/gateway.yaml
nodes.summary: The host gateway file with the routes of one host. It uses JSON syntax, so the scripts can read and write it. GATEWAY_CONFIG in .env names it. A change needs a recreate of gateway, not a restart.

nodes.label: litellm-gateway:local
nodes.summary: The gateway image: the LiteLLM 1.103.0 base image plus the hooks and routers of this repo. docker compose up -d --build builds it from the target gateway. All services except database run it.

nodes.label: gateway
nodes.summary: The LiteLLM proxy that clients call. It holds the routes of the gateway configuration. It runs as the user 1000:1000 with no capability. It starts after database is healthy.
facts: litellm-gateway-1, or litellm with the host override file

nodes.label: database
nodes.summary: Postgres 16, pinned by index digest. It holds the virtual keys, the spend data and the settings from the UI. It listens on 5432 and publishes no port.

nodes.label: litellm_postgres-data
nodes.summary: The named volume of the database at /var/lib/postgresql/data. docker compose down keeps it, and docker compose down -v deletes it. Another Compose project name makes a new, empty volume.

nodes.label: litellm_default
nodes.summary: The project network of the Compose project litellm. The services of the stack join this network. They reach each other by service name, for example http://codex1:4000.

nodes.label: openrouter/*
nodes.summary: A wildcard route to OpenRouter. It reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from .env. A route works only with its key.

nodes.label: local/example-model
nodes.summary: A route to a local OpenAI-compatible server. It reads its address from LOCAL_API_BASE and its key from LOCAL_API_KEY. scripts/sync-local-models.py writes more local routes into the host gateway file.

nodes.label: OpenRouter
nodes.summary: A cloud provider that the default configuration names. The gateway calls it over HTTPS. A request uses the allowance of the provider key.

nodes.label: local endpoint
nodes.summary: An OpenAI-compatible model server of the host, for example llama-swap or vLLM. The example address is http://local-llm.example:8080/v1. The host and the container gateway must both reach the address.

nodes.label: codex1
nodes.summary: The LiteLLM proxy of ChatGPT account 1. It keeps its tokens in state/codex1/ and publishes no port. It is the last account of the default order.

nodes.label: codex2
nodes.summary: The LiteLLM proxy of ChatGPT account 2. It keeps its tokens in state/codex2/ and publishes no port. It is the second account of the default order, and the first with two accounts.

nodes.label: codex3
nodes.summary: The LiteLLM proxy of ChatGPT account 3. It is the first account of the default order. Without a login it stays unhealthy and prints a device code again and again.

nodes.label: codex-router
nodes.summary: An optional quota-aware router for the Codex accounts. It uses the first account with a login that is not blocked. An HTTP 429 moves the request to the next account. The tracked routes do not use it.

nodes.label: copilot
nodes.summary: A LiteLLM proxy with the github_copilot/ provider for one GitHub Copilot account. It runs apart from the gateway, so a stalled key refresh stops only this service. It publishes no port and never starts a device login.

nodes.label: config/gateway.codex.example.yaml
nodes.summary: The tracked template of the Codex routes. It has codex1/, codex2/, codex3/ and codex-auto/ entries for each model. Its fallbacks send codex-auto to codex2, then codex1.
facts: luna, sol, astra, gpt-6-luna, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra

nodes.label: scripts/enable-codex.py
nodes.summary: The script adds the Codex routes to the host gateway file. It stops when a token file of an account is missing. With two logins it writes no codex3 route.

nodes.label: tests/test_codex_routing.py
nodes.summary: The test checks the native Codex routes with synthetic logins. It expects codex3, then codex2, then codex1 with three accounts. With two accounts it expects codex2, then codex1, and no codex3 text.

nodes.label: chatgpt_auth_file.py
nodes.summary: A prototype hook for more than one ChatGPT account in one process. It is off by default. The supported design runs one process for each account.

nodes.label: codex-auto/<model>
nodes.summary: The automatic Codex route. The tracked routes use the native fallback of LiteLLM: codex3, then codex2, then codex1. A host can point these entries at codex-router instead.

nodes.label: codexN/<model>
nodes.summary: The explicit routes codex1/*, codex2/* and codex3/* go to one account each. Use them for previous_response_id and conversation requests. Each route goes to http://codexN:4000/v1.

nodes.label: CODEX_ACCOUNT_ORDER
nodes.summary: The preference order of codex-router. The default is codex3,codex2,codex1. The last account is the final fallback and gets no usage check.

nodes.label: quota_router.py
nodes.summary: The code of codex-router in the image. It runs as quota_router:app under uvicorn. It never refreshes a token.

nodes.label: chatgpt_session_id.py
nodes.summary: The hook gives each request for a chatgpt deployment a stable session id. ChatGPT Codex selects a prompt-cache server by this id. codex-router derives the id with the same function.

nodes.label: tests/test_quota_router.py
nodes.summary: The test checks the router with simulated responses. It covers the order, quota exhaustion, reset and the no-login skip. It also covers the 429 cascade through three accounts.

nodes.label: secrets/codex.env
nodes.summary: The key file of the Codex services, with mode 0600. It holds CODEX_MASTER_KEY, the same value as in .env. Git ignores secrets/.

nodes.label: config/codex.yaml
nodes.summary: The configuration of codex1, codex2 and codex3. It declares the capabilities of the Codex models. Compose mounts it read-only.

nodes.label: state/codexN/auth.json
nodes.summary: The login tokens of each account, with mode 0600. Only the service codexN refreshes its own file. codex-router mounts state/codex2 and state/codex3 read-only.

nodes.label: scripts/login-codex.sh
nodes.summary: The script runs a device-code login in a one-off container of the service codexN. The token goes to state/codexN/. It never imports the refresh token of another client.

nodes.label: scripts/reauth-codex.sh
nodes.summary: The script makes a new login for one account service. It stops the service, backs up auth.json, runs the login and starts the service again. --check prints the state and changes nothing.

nodes.label: chatgpt.com
nodes.summary: ChatGPT Codex answers the requests of the account services. codex-router also asks its usage endpoint. The usage endpoint is not a stable public API.

nodes.label: auth.openai.com
nodes.summary: The login host of the device-code flow. The login prints a URL and a code. You enter the code in a browser with the account of that service.

nodes.label: config/gateway.copilot.example.yaml
nodes.summary: The tracked example of the copilot/ routes. You copy its entries into the host gateway file by hand. No script writes these routes.

nodes.label: copilot/<alias>
nodes.summary: The gateway routes for the Copilot models. Each route goes to http://copilot:4000 with COPILOT_MASTER_KEY. The timeout is 570 seconds.

nodes.label: config/copilot.yaml
nodes.summary: The configuration of the service copilot, with placeholder model ids. A host keeps a copy in .local/config/copilot.yaml. COPILOT_CONFIG in .env names the copy.

nodes.label: secrets/copilot.env
nodes.summary: The key file of the service copilot, with mode 0600. It holds COPILOT_MASTER_KEY, the same value as in .env. Git ignores secrets/.

nodes.label: GITHUB_COPILOT_DEVICE_CODE_URL
nodes.summary: A dead local address in the environment of copilot. With it, a device flow fails at once and the service starts in its usual time. Do not remove it.

nodes.label: state/copilot/
nodes.summary: The token directory, with owner 1000:1000 and mode 0700. access-token is the GitHub OAuth token. api-key.json is the short-lived Copilot key that the service renews.

nodes.label: scripts/login-copilot.sh
nodes.summary: The script runs the device login in a one-off container with no project network. Each code is valid for one minute. The models subcommand lists the model ids of the account.

nodes.label: github.com
nodes.summary: The host of the device login. You open the URL and enter the newest code. Only the login container contacts it.

nodes.label: api.github.com
nodes.summary: The host of the key exchange. The provider sends access-token and gets a new api-key.json. This happens about every 30 minutes.

nodes.label: api.githubcopilot.com
nodes.summary: The Copilot API for the models and the requests. The address can also come from endpoints.api of api-key.json. A model with policy=disabled gets HTTP 400.

nodes.label: .local/compose.host.yaml
nodes.summary: The host override file. It adds a fixed container name and the external network proxy. COMPOSE_FILE lists it last, so its values win.

nodes.label: decision-routes.yaml
nodes.summary: The route table, the thresholds and the question text of the router. DECISION_ROUTES names the file. config/decision-routes.example.yaml is the example with generic model names.

nodes.label: DECISION_ROUTER_ENABLED
nodes.summary: The switch of the decision call. Unset means on. With 0, false, off or no, a request for auto goes to default_model with no decision call.

nodes.label: decision_router.py
nodes.summary: A LiteLLM pre-call hook for the virtual model auto. It is a prototype and off by default. It does not touch requests for another model.

nodes.label: decision-service:8000
nodes.summary: A decision service of the host, not part of this stack. It answers three questions: route, hard and private. The hook waits at most 150 ms.

nodes.label: 1. image part
nodes.summary: The message has an image part. The hook sets image_model. It makes no decision call.

nodes.label: 2. timeout or error
nodes.summary: The decision service times out after 150 ms or fails. The hook sets default_model.

nodes.label: 3. low confidence
nodes.summary: The route confidence is below min_confidence, 0.5 in the example. The hook sets default_model. The log line has review: true.

nodes.label: 4. first matching row
nodes.summary: Otherwise the hook uses the first matching row of routes. A row matches by route and by the hard score.

nodes.label: 5. private guard
nodes.summary: private is 0.5 or more and the model starts with a remote prefix. The hook then sets private.local_model. This is a probability check, not a proof.

nodes.label: local/vision-model
nodes.summary: image_model of the example. A request with an image part goes here. The name is generic.

nodes.label: local/general-model
nodes.summary: default_model and private.local_model of the example. Rules 2, 3 and 5 can set it. The auto entry of the gateway file uses its litellm_params.

nodes.label: row model
nodes.summary: The model of the matching row, for example local/coder-model or local/small-chat-model. The example table maps only to local models. Rule 5 is a guard for later edits.

nodes.label: LiteLLM router
nodes.summary: The router of the gateway gets the rewritten model. It sends the request to the route of that model. A local model goes to a local endpoint.

nodes.label: decision-router.jsonl
nodes.summary: One JSON line for each request, at /state/decision-router.jsonl in the container. It holds the model, the reason, the scores and a hash prefix of the text. It stores an excerpt only when private is below 0.5.

nodes.label: /decision/*
nodes.summary: A pass-through route to the decision service. The client needs a LiteLLM key, and LiteLLM sets the backend key. It is not a model_list entry.

nodes.label: /public-llm/*
nodes.summary: A pass-through route to a paid public service. The request leaves the network. Do not send private data to it.

nodes.label: api.example.com
nodes.summary: The example public service of the pass-through route. It is outside the network of the host. Track its spend in its own console.

nodes.label: topic/*
nodes.summary: One branch for each change. It starts at local-dev and merges into local-dev after review.

nodes.label: upstream
nodes.summary: The upstream LiteLLM repository. It is fetch only, and its push URL is DISABLED. scripts/fetch-upstream.sh fetches one release tag to compare files.

nodes.label: local-dev
nodes.summary: The private integration branch of a host. Its history can hold host values. It never goes to a shared Git server.

nodes.label: origin
nodes.summary: The private integration server, or the source of a target clone. The pre-push hook lets other branches go only to origin.

nodes.label: Git hooks
nodes.summary: pre-commit, pre-merge-commit and pre-push scan each commit, merge and push. scripts/install-hooks.sh installs them. A hook fails closed without Docker or the scanner image.

nodes.label: public-patterns.tsv, public-allow.tsv
nodes.summary: The wording rules of the public check and the accepted exact lines. An accepted line is bound to its path by a SHA-256 hash. An edited line loses its exception.

nodes.label: host-values.deny, host-values.regex
nodes.summary: The host-value rules of the scan. The tracked deny list holds no pattern. The values of one host are in the untracked .local/host-values.deny.

nodes.label: scripts/promote.sh
nodes.summary: The promotion command checks an isolated snapshot and prints a plan by default. --apply makes the local refs, and --push also publishes them. It builds no image and changes no service.

nodes.label: scripts/public_check.sh
nodes.summary: The public check reads the tree, the messages and the identities. It runs scan.sh at level fail on the exact blobs. Matched values stay hidden.

nodes.label: scripts/scan.sh
nodes.summary: The scan stops a secret or a host value before it goes to a remote or into an image. A secret always fails. A host value fails on portable and portable-v* and gives a warning on other branches.
facts: tree, staged, history, image, all, selftest

nodes.label: gitleaks v8.28.0
nodes.summary: The scanner image, pinned by digest in scripts/scan.sh. Each run uses --network none, read-only mounts and --redact. With the image present, the scan needs no network.

nodes.label: portable
nodes.summary: Snapshot commits with the files of local-dev and no development history. The previous snapshot is the only parent. Only portable and its release tags go to a shared Git server.

nodes.label: portable-vX.Y.Z
nodes.summary: An annotated release tag on a snapshot. scripts/build.sh uses X.Y.Z in the image tag. An existing tag stops a later run with the same version.

nodes.label: github
nodes.summary: The default publication remote. A push needs an approved plan of scripts/promote.sh. The remote may hold only HEAD, portable and portable-v* tags.

nodes.label: CI pipeline
nodes.summary: A pipeline calls the same scripts as a host. The repo gives no pipeline file for one CI product. A push must start only from portable or a portable-v* tag.

nodes.label: scripts/check-prereqs.sh
nodes.summary: The script checks the host tools before an install or a pipeline run. It stops with exit code 1 when a hard requirement is missing. Node 24 is a hard requirement.

nodes.label: scripts/build.sh
nodes.summary: The script starts a build with docker buildx bake -f docker-bake.hcl. It reads the revision and the commit time from Git. It refuses a dirty tree for release and pushes only with --push.

nodes.label: LiteLLM 1.103.0 base image
nodes.summary: The upstream image ghcr.io/berriai/litellm, pinned by index digest in Dockerfile and docker-bake.hcl. BASE_IMAGE names a mirror with the same digest. The hooks stop a version that is not in TESTED_VERSIONS.

nodes.label: python:3.13-slim-bookworm
nodes.summary: A Python image, pinned by digest. It installs pytest for the test target only. It is not part of the gateway image.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: The stages addons, gateway, smoke, pytest and test. The final stage gateway has no RUN step. The stage addons sets owner, mode and file times of the hooks and routers.

nodes.label: docker-bake.hcl
nodes.summary: The build definition with the targets gateway, smoke, test and release. It sets the tag <LITELLM_VERSION>-p<PORTABLE_VERSION> and the labels. The pipeline file holds no build logic.

nodes.label: smoke
nodes.summary: The target starts python -c pass on the gateway image. It fails when the hooks stop an untested LiteLLM version. scripts/build.sh builds it before gateway and release.

nodes.label: gateway (target)
nodes.summary: The default target for the host platform. It loads the image into the local image store. Its tag is litellm-gateway:1.103.0-p<portable version>.

nodes.label: test
nodes.summary: The target runs pytest on tests/ inside the gateway image, with no network in that step. The build fails when a test fails. It exports no image.

nodes.label: release
nodes.summary: The target builds linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. It needs a builder with the docker-container driver. The output is a push or an OCI archive.

nodes.label: litellm-gateway:1.103.0-pX.Y.Z
nodes.summary: The image of scripts/build.sh with labels for the revision, the version and the time. Without a release tag at HEAD, the portable version uses git describe. Compose uses it only when GATEWAY_IMAGE names it.

nodes.label: <registry>/litellm-gateway
nodes.summary: The registry of a released image. A deployment uses the index digest, not the tag. GATEWAY_IMAGE then names the image with its digest.

nodes.label: OCI archive
nodes.summary: scripts/build.sh --oci FILE release writes both platforms to one archive. Two builds of the same revision give the same index digest without provenance.

nodes.label: .env.example
nodes.summary: The tracked template of .env with empty secrets. Do not copy it to .env: Compose refuses to start with its empty secrets. The host settings in it are comment lines.

nodes.label: scripts/create-env.py
nodes.summary: The script makes .env from .env.example with new random secrets and mode 0600. It refuses to replace a .env that exists. It prints key names only.

nodes.label: compose.yaml
nodes.summary: The base Compose file with gateway and database. It sets name: litellm and has no external network and no fixed container name.

nodes.label: compose.codex.yaml
nodes.summary: The optional Compose file with codex1, codex2, codex3 and codex-router. It is off by default. COMPOSE_FILE or -f adds it.

nodes.label: compose.copilot.yaml
nodes.summary: The optional Compose file with the service copilot. It is off by default. Add it to COMPOSE_FILE only after the login.

nodes.label: config/copilot.yaml
nodes.summary: The tracked configuration of copilot, with placeholder model ids. A host copies it to .local/config/copilot.yaml and keeps the ids of its account.

nodes.label: scripts/sync-local-models.py
nodes.summary: The script reads the model list of each local endpoint and writes one route for each model. It writes nothing when an endpoint does not answer.

nodes.label: scripts/enable-anthropic.py
nodes.summary: The script adds the anthropic/* route and writes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY into .env. It reads the credential from a hidden prompt.

nodes.label: scripts/gateway_config.py
nodes.summary: The shared code that finds and writes the host gateway file. It writes a temporary file and then replaces the target. It stops when GATEWAY_CONFIG points into config/.

nodes.label: docs/diagrams/architecture-graph.json
nodes.summary: The tracked graph source of this page. It holds generic names only. Each node names the tracked files that prove it.

nodes.label: scripts/build-architecture-html.py
nodes.summary: The builder writes one self-contained HTML page from the graph source. With --overlay it writes the private edition, and only to a path under .local/. --check compares the build with the file on disk.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.html
nodes.summary: The public edition of this page. It is tracked and holds no host value. It works from file:// with no network request.

nodes.label: .local/config/copilot.yaml
nodes.summary: The host copy of the configuration of copilot. It keeps only the model ids of the account. COPILOT_CONFIG in .env names it.

nodes.label: .local/host-values.deny
nodes.summary: The host values of one host for the scan. Create it on each host that works on local-dev. A promotion clone needs a copy of it.

nodes.label: .local/diagrams/overlay.json
nodes.summary: The private overlay of this page. It replaces labels, summaries and values by node id and adds host-only nodes. It holds no secret.

nodes.label: .local/diagrams/architecture-local.html
nodes.summary: The private edition of this page, with the values of one host. Git ignores it. Its header shows a banner for the private edition.

nodes.label: secrets/
nodes.summary: codex.env and copilot.env, the keys of the optional services, with mode 0600. Git ignores the directory. Back it up separately.

nodes.label: state/
nodes.summary: The login tokens of the optional services: state/codexN/auth.json and state/copilot/. Git ignores the directory. The login containers and the services write it.

nodes.label: docker compose
nodes.summary: Compose merges the files of COMPOSE_FILE in order. A later file changes the values of an earlier one. It fills each ${VAR} from .env.

steps.text: A client sends a request with a LiteLLM key to 127.0.0.1:4321. This is the only published port.
For a public address, a reverse proxy forwards HTTPS to litellm:4000. The proxy is an option of the host.
The gateway reads its keys from .env. It loads the default routes from config/gateway.example.yaml.
A host replaces the default routes with .local/config/gateway.yaml. GATEWAY_CONFIG in .env names the file.
The gateway keeps keys and spend in Postgres. The data stays in the volume litellm_postgres-data.
The gateway selects a route by the model name. The route sends the request to a provider.
The optional services are off by default. The gateway reaches them by service name on the project network.
All services except database run one image. docker compose up -d --build builds it.

tours.name: Codex accounts and the route order

steps.text: Each ChatGPT account has its own LiteLLM process. Each process keeps its own tokens.
A device-code login writes state/codexN/auth.json. Only the service of that account refreshes the file.
scripts/enable-codex.py adds the Codex routes to the host gateway file. It counts the complete logins.
codexN/<model> goes to one account. Use it for a request that continues an earlier response.
codex-auto/<model> uses the native fallback. It tries codex3, then codex2, then codex1.
codex-router is the alternative for codex-auto. It checks the usage of each account and skips a blocked account.
A stable session id keeps one conversation on one prompt-cache server. The router uses the same id function.
Two tests check the order with synthetic logins and simulated responses. They need no real account.
The login comes first, in a one-off container. You enter the newest code in a browser.
The login writes access-token and api-key.json. The service renews api-key.json about every 30 minutes.
The service reads its model list and its key. The dead device-code address stops a login at the start.
You copy the copilot/ routes into the host gateway file. Each route goes to http://copilot:4000.
A request for copilot/<alias> goes through the gateway to the service. The service calls the Copilot API.
A client sends the model auto. The pre-call hook of the gateway handles only this model.
A host turns the hook on in its own files. The tracked defaults do not load it.
Rule 1 sends a message with an image part to image_model. It makes no decision call.
The hook asks the decision service and waits at most 150 ms. Rule 2 gives default_model after a timeout or an error.
Rule 3 sends a low confidence to default_model. Rule 4 takes the first matching row of the table.
Rule 5 keeps private text on a local model. It is a probability check, not a proof.
The router of the gateway sends the request to the chosen model. The hook writes one log line.
Pass-through routes are a separate path. They expose a backend behind the LiteLLM key.

tours.name: From a topic branch to a released image

steps.text: Each change starts on a topic branch. It merges into local-dev after review.
The Git hooks scan each commit, merge and push. A secret always fails the scan.
local-dev goes only to the private server origin. upstream is fetch only.
scripts/promote.sh checks a snapshot of local-dev. The public check reads the tree, the messages and the identities.
The snapshot goes to portable with a release tag. A push to github needs an approved plan.
scripts/build.sh builds from docker-bake.hcl. The base image is pinned by index digest.
smoke runs before gateway and release. test runs the tests inside the image.
A release builds two platforms. A deployment uses the index digest of the image.
scripts/create-env.py makes .env with new secrets. Git ignores .env.
COMPOSE_FILE lists the Compose files in order. The host override file comes last.
The gateway loads the example routes by default. GATEWAY_CONFIG selects the host gateway file.
Three scripts write routes through scripts/gateway_config.py. They never write a tracked file.
A host keeps its Copilot model list in .local/config/copilot.yaml. COPILOT_CONFIG names it.
secrets/ and state/ hold keys and tokens. .local/host-values.deny holds the host values for the scan.
This page comes from a tracked graph source. A private overlay under .local/ makes the edition of one host.
